question: In the Apple Valley Fire Protection District's 2024 RFP for GASB 75 OPEB actuarial services, as of which dates must the actuary deliver the biennial OPEB valuations and the biennial roll-forward updates?
gold_answer: Biennial valuations as of June 30, 2024, June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2028; biennial roll-forward updates as of June 30, 2025, June 30, 2027 and June 30, 2029.
gold_passage: Deliver OPEB related biennial valuations as of June 30, 2024, June 30, 2026, and June 30, 2028. | Deliver OPEB biennial roll-forward updates as of June 30, 2025, June 30, 2027, and June 30, 2029.
notes: Scope of Work items 2 and 3. Recommended contributions are also requested for FY 2025-2030 (item 4).

question: According to the questions and answers for OCERS' October 2022 custody services RFP, what flat fee does OCERS currently pay its custodian, and what is the current securities lending fee split?
gold_answer: A flat fee of $580,000 covering custody, accounting, cash management, performance reporting and risk report services (all services in Section 3 Scope of Services); the securities lending fee split is 80% OCERS / 20% State Street.

question: In the Contra Costa County Employees' Retirement Association (CCCERA) April 2018 master custodian RFP, how many copies of the proposal must be submitted, and for how long must the proposal remain a firm and irrevocable offer?
gold_answer: One (1) original proposal, four (4) hard copies and one (1) copy in electronic form; the proposal must be a firm and irrevocable offer good for one year from the proposal due date (due 5:00 p.m. PT, Friday, May 25, 2018).

question: In the Indiana Public Retirement System (INPRS) RFP 24-05 for audit services, which firm has provided INPRS's external audit services and since when, and what limit does INPRS's procurement policy place on contract length?
gold_answer: RSM has provided external audit services since 2014. The procurement policy in the INPRS Board Governance Manual limits contract length to 10 years and requires new bids at least every 10 years. (Before 2014 the Indiana State Board of Accounts performed the audits.)

question: A county 457(b) deferred compensation plan RFP subject to the rules of the New York State Deferred Compensation Board states a minimum deferral amount required by the Model Plan. What is that minimum, and within how many business days must participant deferrals be invested?
gold_answer: $260 for any plan year (Model Plan Section 3.2(a)); deferrals must be invested no later than two (2) business days following receipt (Model Plan Section 4.1). The issuer is the Monroe County (NY) Deferred Compensation Plan / Committee (RFP dated August 4, 2023).
gold_passage: The Model Plan requires a minimum deferral amount to be $260 for any plan year. | invested, according to the participant’s investment directions, no later than two (2) business days following receipt thereof, in the appropriate investment funds.
notes: Uniqueness checked: '$260' and 'Deferred Compensation Board' appear only in the Monroe County file.

question: One deferred compensation recordkeeping RFP requires vendors to have at least 500,000 participant plan accounts on their defined contribution recordkeeping system. question: A retirement system is hiring a consultant to oversee the replacement of its current pension administration system, called V3. What minimum umbrella liability and professional liability insurance does that RFP require?
gold_answer: Umbrella Liability: $5M per occurrence / $5M aggregate; Professional Liability: $2M per occurrence / $3M aggregate. (Also required: Commercial General Liability $2M/$2M, Automobile $1M/$2M, Workers Compensation $1M/$1M.) Issuer: OCERS, September 2023 Pension Administration Project Oversight and Consultation Services RFP.
gold_passage: This solution will replace their current system, V3. | Umbrella Liability: $5M per occurrence, $5M aggregate | Professional Liability: $2M per occurrence, $3M aggregate

question: What minimum qualifications must an audit firm meet in the Kern County Employees' Retirement Association (KCERA) RFP for audit services?
gold_answer: (1) Professional public accounting firm organized at least on a regional basis providing audit and attest services; (2) within the last five years, at least five audits of defined benefit pension plans with assets over $2 billion; (3) experience auditing equity securities (domestic and foreign), fixed income, real estate, alternative investments, commodities and securities lending; (4) an established office in the United States; (5) independent, licensed by and in good standing with California under the Accountancy Act; (6) Engagement Partner (and signing partner) located in the U.S. with at least 10 years of public accounting experience including DB pension plan audits, California-licensed CPA; (7) Engagement Manager located in the U.S. with at least 5 years of public accounting experience including DB plan audits, CPA licensed in a U.S. state; (8) On-Site Audit Supervisor located in the U.S. with at least 3 years of auditing experience including DB plan audits, CPA licensed in a U.S. state; (9) Engagement Manager and Supervisor available for consultations and in-person meetings throughout the year.
gold_passage: The firm must have conducted, within the last five (5) years, at least five (5) audits of defined benefit pension plans with assets that exceeded two billion dollars ($2,000,000,000). | must be located in the United States and have at least ten (10) years of experience in public accounting. | have at least five (5) years of experience in public accounting. | have at least three (3) years of professional auditing experience.
notes: From Attachment 2, Minimum and Desirable Qualifications Certification. Desirable (not minimum) qualifications include partner/manager having done at least two audits of DB plans over $3 billion in the last five years. Section I.C also lists State Controller qualification guidelines.

question: What minimum qualifications must a proposing firm certify in the City of Temple City's 2020 RFP for 457 plan administration and recordkeeping services?
gold_answer: (1) At least 5 years of experience administering governmental 457 plans and currently providing sole-provider administration to at least five 457 plans with assets under $25 million; (2) no front-end or back-end charges and no restrictions/penalties on plan- or participant-initiated transfers or withdrawals (except capital preservation equity wash/put provisions and fund short-term trading fees); (3) full disclosure of all fund expense and revenue sharing arrangements, including fixed/general account products; (4) full disclosure of expenses and revenue for any service (platform fees, managed accounts, advice, financial planning, brokerage); (5) agree not to sell/promote products not affiliated with the Plan without written City authorization; (6) be qualified to do business in California and Temple City upon award; (7) offer a self-directed brokerage option; (8) be able to transition and continue administration of existing loans; (9) representatives attend City meetings in person as requested (no more than once per year); (10) knowledge of and compliance with applicable County, California and federal regulations; (11) RFP terms remain in place through negotiations and the final contract unless waived in writing.
gold_passage: must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience administering governmental Section 457 deferred compensation plans and must currently provide sole-provider administration to a minimum of five (5) Section 457 deferred compensation retirement plans with an asset size of less than $25 million. | The organization must be able to offer a self-directed brokerage option. | The Proposing Firm must be willing to have representatives attend City meetings in person as requested (no more than once per year).

question: What scope of services does the Kern County Employees' Retirement Association (KCERA) 2024 actuarial audit services RFP require?
gold_answer: A full actuarial audit of the assumptions, methods, calculations and experience used in KCERA's valuation, in two parts: (1) a peer review audit of the Actuarial Experience Study for July 1, 2019 - June 30, 2022 and the Review of Economic Actuarial Assumptions as of June 30, 2022 - evaluating the data (including comparison of census data), reconciling discrepancies with the consulting actuary, and evaluating the recommended economic and non-economic assumptions; and (2) a parallel valuation (independent reproduction) of the June 30, 2023 valuation, including the SRBR valuation and GASB 67 valuation, using the consulting actuary's assumptions and methods and reproducing all work without relying on the consulting actuary, with reconciliation of discrepancies. Results of both are to be communicated to the consulting actuary before completion of the June 30, 2024 valuation.
gold_passage: KCERA seeks one qualified actuarial firm to perform a full actuarial audit of assumptions, methods, calculations, and experience used in KCERA’s actuarial valuation. The 2019-2022 experience study and the June 30, 2023, valuation will be subject to a full actuarial audit. | ACTUARY shall conduct a parallel valuation (independent reproduction of the detailed valuation results) of KCERA’s June 30, 2023, valuation, including the SRBR valuation and GASB 67 valuation. | ACTUARY shall reproduce all work and not rely on the work of KCERA’s consulting actuary.
notes: Exhibit B - Scope of Services. KCERA's consulting actuary is Segal Consulting (engaged through April 1, 2025). Contract term is one year; evaluation weights are Experience 30%, Personnel 25%, Communication 25%, Cost 20%.

question: What project oversight services does OCERS require from the consultant in its 2023 RFP for Pension Administration Project Oversight and Consultation Services?
gold_answer: Developing and reviewing key project management deliverables covering: (1) planning (requirements definition, IT strategic roadmap, solutions design); (2) writing the RFP(s) for the software/services; (3) coordinating the procurement and selection process; (4) oversight of the new PAS design, development, testing, training and implementation, coordinating with OCERS' EPMO; (5) establishing a sign-off process; (6) project deliverables and reports/metrics (needs assessment, staffing plan, IT roadmap, budget, vendor management, SOWs, data conversion, test plans, UAT, schedule/cutover); (7) project methodology, planning and scheduling; (8) project communications; (9) project issues management/escalation; (10) project risk; (11) change control; (12) quality/testing procedures; (13) other project management issues. Services must be provided on-site, and a monthly oversight status report goes to the Steering Committee and the Board.
